body: I know that adding a new architecture can take time, but it would be helpful if you stopped publishing the `universal-darwin` version of the compiled gem until you've added Arm support. With MacOS dropping 32-bit support in 10.15 and the advent of Arm Macs, Apple now uses "universal" to mean x86_64 and arm64. When I use bundler to install this gem with a lock file that has `arm64-darwin` as a platform on my Arm Mac, it sees "universal" and uses the current definition to download your "universal" build. Unfortunately, this doesn't work, but allowing it to install and build from source does.

body:
Is there anything that I can do to help this issue towards resolution?  This issue is quite important for us, at least, as it makes installation of our code (which depends on `grpc`) an annoyingly fiddly task on an arm64 Mac, as the user has to install `grpc` manually from source, and then install our gem on top -- which is a pretty bad UX.

The interim fix -- pending support for adding arm64 into the build, which I totally understand is probably not trivial -- could potentially be as simple as replacing the `universal` label with `x86_64` on the Darwin arch spec.  Forcing the (probably very few, by now) PPC users to build `grpc` from source is a reasonable trade-off, IMO, in order to allow arm64 users to also build from source, as compared to the current situation where `grpc` fails with a fairly inscrutable error message at runtime for arm64 users.

If a PR for the above would be accepted, please let me know and I'll whip something up ASAP.

Worth noting that @mpalmer's suggested interim fix is exactly what the google-protobuf gem (which also does not have a working darwin-arm64 native gem yet) has done since v3.19 (https://rubygems.org/gems/google-protobuf/versions), so it seems sensible!

A lot of issues are being created on this project all to work around the same problem (https://github.com/grpc/grpc/issues/24846, https://github.com/grpc/grpc/issues/29100, etc). Is there a maintainer I can sponsor or some equivalent who can make progress on this?

Mac arm should be supported now, though it takes some time to build the extension.
Can you verify if latest releases work for you?

Custom strip invalidates the signature, caused the arm64-darwin gem failed to run on M1 macs.
Error in mac console: `Exception Type:        EXC_BAD_ACCESS (SIGKILL (Code Signature Invalid))`

Warning in gem build log:
```
# linking shared-object grpc/grpc_c.bundle
# Stripping grpc_c.bundle
# /opt/osxcross/target/bin/aarch64-apple-darwin20.2-strip: warning: changes being made to the file will invalidate the code signature in: /Users/jeff/work/ruby/grpc/tmp/arm64-darwin/grpc_c/3.2.0/grpc_c.bundle
```

Custom stripping is not really needed (any more), this diff removes it from `src/ruby/ext/grpc/extconf.rb`, the [gem artifact](https://console.cloud.google.com/storage/browser/grpc-testing-kokoro-prod/test_result_public/prod/grpc/core/pull_request/linux/grpc_distribtests_ruby/19833/20230708-181642/github/grpc/artifacts?pageState=(%22StorageObjectListTable%22:(%22f%22:%22%255B%255D%22))&prefix=&forceOnObjectsSortingFiltering=false) size didn't change and arm64-darwin gem runs fine on M1 mac.
